Subject: Renewal request — term rework + 25% capacity uptick

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the catch-up last week. CloudWave is ready to move forward with renewal, but we need two items addressed in the paperwork before procurement can route for signature:

1) Shift the MSA term from 12 to 24 months (with the existing termination provisions unchanged).
2) Add a 25% capacity uptick (order-form line item) effective on renewal date and confirm billing proration for the partial month.

Attached is our renewal request PDF and a preliminary redline from our legal team (simple markup of exhibit B and order form).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept a 24-month term, and whether the uptime/credits language needs any change for the longer term? Also please confirm who on your side will handle an order-form amendment and whether we need a new Exhibit D for the capacity bump.

We'd like to close before the end of the quarter.

Thanks,

Thanks for the ping, Jordan. I reviewed the customer's redline and did a targeted pass. High-level:

1) Term change: we can accept 24 months but need to modify the auto-renewal notice window from 60 days to 90 days in the MSA, or explicitly carve out this renewal as non-auto-renewing for the first renewal term. Customer redline didn't address notice windows; I'm proposing the 90-day language to protect both parties (we've seen administrative lag on their side).

2) SLA / credits: no change required to the SLA definitions. However, to avoid ambiguity over scaling SLAs with longer terms, add a single-sentence clarifier in Exhibit G: "SLA terms remain as defined; credits apply per incident regardless of term length." Simple insertion, non-substantive.

3) Order form & proration: the order form needs an explicit proration formula. I've drafted the clause: "If a capacity increase is effective mid-billing cycle, charges for the increased capacity will be prorated based on the number of days the increased capacity was in effect in that billing cycle." Laura, please confirm the invoicing label (line item code) we should use.

4) Exhibit D: not necessary — we can fold the capacity uptick as an amendment to the existing order form. That keeps signing simple.

I've attached a clean tracked changes file (CW_MSA-Redline_Response.docx) that accepts the term length but inserts the 90-day notice and the proration language. I'm not asking to renegotiate indemnity or data terms — those are unchanged.

If the commercial team approves Ben's proposed pricing (Ben — please reply inline with the discount band), we can produce a single redline for CloudWave and request signature.

I'll be available for a 20-minute call at 16:00 PST if you want to triage final language before we send.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Legal Operations — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
